sources.title: William Morris and wallpaper design
sources.coverage: article text lines 34–63 read; no claim of museum-image pixel inspection
facts: Close observation of nature is stylised rather than literal transcription.
Later patterns interweave foreground and background foliage.
sources.project_inference: Use repeatable curved stem graphs and layered botanical silhouettes rather than unconstrained random scatter.

sources.title: Acanthus wallpaper B32b.2
sources.coverage: catalogue text lines39–63 read; image URL located, not counted as visual study
sources.project_inference: Build a reusable controlled motif cell; game dimensions and code formulas are proposed engineering parameters, not historical Morris algorithms.

sources.title: Wool on linen collection entries F335 and F430
facts: F335 combines alternating stylised flower clumps over arabesque stems and leaves.
F430 peacock is attributed toWebb; vine pattern toMorris.
sources.project_inference: Separate large motif from small interstitial pattern; preserve collaborative attribution for fauna.

sources.title: The Hare, study for The Forest tapestry NT2900066.2
sources.coverage: catalogue text620–664 read; date inconsistencies within page retained as caution
facts: The Forest tapestry described asMorris,Webb,Dearle collaboration.
Scaling gridlines used for tapestry cartoon.
sources.project_inference: Animal silhouettes should be carefully observed, then integrated with ornamental foliage; do not attribute every animal drawing toMorris.

sources.title: Philip Webb: a new vision for domestic space
